title: add-region-harbor-rbac-templates-and-kms-assertion-logshipper
author: Maya Rodriguez
release_notes: Introduce region-harbor RBAC templates, tenant-scoped KMS assertion headers, and an audit log shipper that produces immutable envelopes. No runtime behavior change for existing tenants; opt-in via config flag.
description: Motivation: customers asked for a simple way to guarantee that tenant traffic is pinned to a declared region and that KMS usage and audit records carry an immutable assertion bundle for downstream compliance. This PR introduces a small, opinionated policy kit called 'region-harbor' (RBAC v2 templates + bindings), a lightweight KMS assertion header middleware, and a logshipper that wraps audit events in signed immutable envelopes for retention and replay. Goals: 1) provide deployable RBAC v2 role templates that enforce region-scoped operator and service principals, 2) emit a per-request KMS assertion header showing the key origin and geo-affinity, 3) produce auditable envelopes (HMAC-signed, timestamped) so downstream collectors can verify tamper-resistance. Implementation summary: added RBAC templates under pkg/rbac/templates/region_harbor.yaml, policy compiler helpers (pkg/rbac/compiler/region_harbor.go), KMS assertion middleware (internal/http/middleware/kms_assertion.go) that injects X-Redwood-KMS-Assertion, and audit logshipper component (observability/audit/logshipper/envelope.go) which signs events with the service HMAC key and attaches an envelope id. This is opt-in behind feature flag feature.region_harbor and a tenant-level flag tenant.config.region_harbor_enabled. Checklist: - [x] RBAC templates and tests - [x] Middleware and unit tests - [x] Audit envelope format spec and integration tests - [x] End-to-end smoke verifying envelope verification in audit-collector - [x] Documentation in docs/compliance/region_harbor.md Migrations/compatibility: existing RBAC and KMS flows remain unchanged until tenants opt in. The envelope format is additive and backwards-compatible with current audit event schema. Security considerations: HMAC keys are stored in KMS and retrieved by the logshipper with restricted IAM. The middleware emits only attestations about the KMS key id and region affinity; no plaintext key material is logged. Related: references Linear ENG-2146 (region-harbor spike) and SEC-88 (audit immutable envelopes).

review_comments: Asha Patel: Can we clarify the attack model for the envelope signer? Who rotates the HMAC key and how is key compromise handled?

Maya Rodriguez (author): The HMAC key lifecycle is managed by KMS. We've added a rotation handler in envelope.go that re-keys and stamps previous envelopes with a key-version header. If compromise is detected operators can mark a key as revoked and the collector will reject new envelopes signed with it.
Connor Liu: The RBAC templates look good but please add an example that shows a cross-zone operator denied scenario (I want to include it in the policy docs).
Maya Rodriguez: Added a deny example in docs and an integration test that simulates operator claims from mismatched regions.
Diego Morales: CI had a flaky test in audit-collector verification; can we add retry/backoff instead of sleeping?
Maya Rodriguez: Reworked the test to use a polling helper with an exponential backoff. Flake resolved.
Security review (automated): flagged missing telemetry for envelope verification failures - added metric audit.envelope.verify.failures
Maya Rodriguez: Added metric and alert rule in observability/alerts/audit_envelope_rules.yaml

notes_for_ops: Feature is gated. To enable for a tenant set tenant.config.region_harbor_enabled=true and ensure the tenant has a configured cmk in the same geozone. The logshipper requires read access to HMAC keys in KMS and an alert is provided for envelope verification failures.
test_plan: Unit tests for templates and middleware; integration test that provisions a test tenant with region_harbor_enabled and asserts that audit events arrive wrapped in a signed envelope and that the collector can verify signatures. Also a negative test where an envelope is tampered and verification fails.
acknowledgements: Thanks to the security guild for threat-model review and to the observability team for helping design the envelope schema.
